object_context: Post-calibration analytic Riemann-Hypothesis child atom. RH-ANA-001 proved only a criterion-falsifier fact: long finite Li-positive prefixes can miss off-critical symmetric data. RH-ANA-002 therefore localizes the genuinely zeta-specific all-index obstruction. Before inventing any inequality, compare the arithmetic Li decomposition, finite-prefix/zero-free-region theorems, and current zeta zero-free methods to determine which proposed prime-side uniform bound is strictly weaker than RH and which merely restates the root in asymptotic form. No mathematical candidate exists yet.
structural_coordinates: Li positivity is an exact all-index RH criterion; the finite-prefix surrogate has already failed as a global certificate on an exact symmetric multiset calibration
for the zeta specialization the arithmetic explicit formula separates each Li coefficient into an archimedean contribution, a finite-place contribution, and the pole term
Lagarias gives the archimedean contribution unconditionally with dominant growth one-half n log n plus a linear term and bounded remainder
Lagarias identifies the finite-place contribution unconditionally with an incomplete Li coefficient using zeros up to height sqrt(n), up to O(sqrt(n) log n)
under RH the incomplete Li coefficient is O(sqrt(n) log n), whereas if RH fails Lagarias states that it is sometimes exponentially large in n
therefore a uniform polynomial-growth theorem for the full finite-place contribution would be root-strength rather than a cheap intermediate target
if RH is known only up to height T, Lagarias' small-finite-place bound propagates only to a finite n-range of order T^2/(log T)^2; finite verification remains finite

Brown proves a quantitative two-way relation between finitely many Li inequalities and zero-free regions, so finite Li information naturally licenses partial exclusion geometry rather than the full critical-line conclusion
Freitas supplies Li-type criteria parameterized by zero-free half-planes/strips, providing a second source for a graded implication ladder rather than a binary finite-prefix/root jump
the zeta finite-place formula contains regularized prime sums; the subtraction/cutoff cancellation is proof-critical and forbids naive termwise positivity or absolute-value domination
current explicit zeta zero-free regions near Re(s)=1 are genuine zeta-specific input but remain far weaker than RH and therefore serve as partial-control calibration rather than a root bridge
the desired child target must be graded: stronger than currently known partial zero exclusion but demonstrably weaker than an all-n polynomial bound that would already force RH
equivalent_formulations: every nontrivial zero rho of zeta(s) has Re(rho)=1/2

global certification requires a uniform coverage or coercivity mechanism
